### AlteryxConnectBase

File: `src/api/alteryx-base.ts`

Description: Base class for alteryx agent (and setup) which provides headers and proxy handling. AlteryxConnectBase

Properties:
- `_apiHeaders: object = { ...this._headers, "Content-Type": "application/json", }` — Http headers used for onboarding message. AlteryxConnectBase
- ``_headers: object = { Accept: "*/*", "X-Powered-By": "meowz", "User-Agent": `${AYX_NAME} (${AYX_VERSION})`, }``
- `_multipartFormData: object = { ...this._headers, "Content-Type": "multipart/form-data; boundary=--alteryx", }`
- `_multipartHeaders: object = { ...this._headers, "Content-Type": "multipart/mixed; boundary=alteryxmessage", }` — Http headers used for /exchange endpoint handling. AlteryxConnectBase
- `_octetStreamHeaders: object = { ...this._headers, "Content-Type": "application/octet-stream", }`
- `_proxyHttpAgent: any` — This is a https proxy agent which is used in the fetch commands if the HTTP\_PROXY variable is configured. AlteryxConnectBase
- `_urlEncodedHeaders: object = { ...this._headers, "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", }` — Http headers used to register the client assertion and acquire the /exchange token. AlteryxConnectBase

Methods:
- `HttpAction(: { verb: "GET" | "POST" | "PATCH" | "PUT" | "DELETE"; gateway: string; baseUrl: string; authorization: string; body?: Object; message?: string; octetStream?: boo…): Promise<Object | undefined>` — Performs an HTTP request with comprehensive options for different API scenarios. This method handles all HTTP communication with the Alteryx API, supporting various content types, response formats, and error handling strategies.

### AuthBase

File: `src/api/auth-base.ts`
Extends: `AlteryxConnectBase`

Properties:

- `_oauthResponse?: any`
- `_publicKey: any`
- `_apiHeaders: object = { ...this._headers, "Content-Type": "application/json", }` — Http headers used for onboarding message. AlteryxConnectBase
- ``_headers: object = { Accept: "*/*", "X-Powered-By": "meowz", "User-Agent": `${AYX_NAME} (${AYX_VERSION})`, }``
- `_multipartFormData: object = { ...this._headers, "Content-Type": "multipart/form-data; boundary=--alteryx", }`
- `_multipartHeaders: object = { ...this._headers, "Content-Type": "multipart/mixed; boundary=alteryxmessage", }` — Http headers used for /exchange endpoint handling. AlteryxConnectBase
- `_octetStreamHeaders: object = { ...this._headers, "Content-Type": "application/octet-stream", }`
- `_proxyHttpAgent: any` — This is a https proxy agent which is used in the fetch commands if the HTTP\_PROXY variable is configured. AlteryxConnectBase
- `_urlEncodedHeaders: object = { ...this._headers, "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", }` — Http headers used to register the client assertion and acquire the /exchange token. AlteryxConnectBase

Methods:
- `AcquireToken(): Promise<boolean>`
- `GetGateway(): string`
- `GetTenant(): string`
- `GetToken(): Promise<string>`
- `RenewToken(): Promise<boolean>` — Renews the authentication token if necessary. This method implements the token renewal logic: If a token exists, it attempts to validate it If validation fails, it clears the token and prepares for renewal If no valid token exists, it acquires a new one It validates the newly acquired token This ensures the SDK always has a valid token for API requests.
- `ValidateToken(): Promise<boolean>` — Validates the current access token. Note: This method currently performs a basic validation check. The commented code shows a more comprehensive JWT validation approach that may be implemented in the future.
- `HttpAction(: { verb: "GET" | "POST" | "PATCH" | "PUT" | "DELETE"; gateway: string; baseUrl: string; authorization: string; body?: Object; message?: string; octetStream?: boo…): Promise<Object | undefined>` — Performs an HTTP request with comprehensive options for different API scenarios. This method handles all HTTP communication with the Alteryx API, supporting various content types, response formats, and error handling strategies.

Description: The Collection Management API provides a means form managing Collections. {CollectionManagementClientV1}

- `_authenticator: TokenRotation`

- `AddUserToCollection(collectionId: string, addUsersContract: SDKModels.AddUserContract): Promise<SDKModels.CollectionView>` — Add a user to a Collection CollectionManagementClient

- `GetCollection(collectionId: string): Promise<SDKModels.CollectionView>` — Retrieve a collection record CollectionManagementClient
- `GetCollections(view?: "Default" | "Full"): Promise<Array<SDKModels.ReducedCollectionView>>` — Retrieve all accessible collection records CollectionManagementClient
- `RemoveInsightFromCollection(collectionId: string, insightId: string): Promise<SDKModels.CollectionView>` — Remove an insight from a Collection CollectionManagementClient
- `RemoveScheduleFromCollection(collectionId: string, scheduleId: string): Promise<SDKModels.CollectionView>` — Remove a schedule from a Collection CollectionManagementClient
- `RemoveUserFromCollection(collectionId: string, userId: string): Promise<SDKModels.CollectionView>` — Remove a user from a Collection CollectionManagementClient
- `RemoveUserGroupFromCollection(collectionId: string, userGroupId: string): Promise<SDKModels.CollectionView>` — Remove a userGroup from a Collection CollectionManagementClient
- `RemoveWorkflowFromCollection(collectionId: string, appId: string): Promise<SDKModels.CollectionView>` — Remove a workflow from a Collection CollectionManagementClient
- `UpdateCollection(collectionId: string, updateCollectionContract: SDKModels.UpdateCollectionContract): Promise<SDKModels.CollectionView>` — Update an existing collection to change the name or owner CollectionManagementClient
- `UpdateCollectionUserGroupPermissions(collectionId: string, userGroupId: string, updatePermissionsContract: SDKModels.UpdatePermissionsContract): Promise<SDKModels.CollectionView>` — Update a collection userGroups permissions CollectionManagementClient
- `UpdateCollectionUserPermissions(collectionId: string, userId: string, updatePermissionsContract: SDKModels.UpdatePermissionsContract): Promise<SDKModels.CollectionView>` — For Windows Authentication configured Server instances, provide the Active Directory Sid for the userId parameter. Update a collection users permissions. CollectionManagementClient

Methods:

- `GetTenant(): string`

This method implements the token renewal logic: If a token exists, it attempts to validate it If validation fails, it clears the token and prepares for renewal If no valid token exists, it acquires a new one It validates the newly acquired token This ensures the SDK always has a valid token for API requests.
- `ValidateToken(): Promise<boolean>` — Validates the current access token. Note: This method currently performs a basic validation check. The commented code shows a more comprehensive JWT validation approach that may be implemented in the future.
- `HttpAction(: { verb: "GET" | "POST" | "PATCH" | "PUT" | "DELETE"; gateway: string; baseUrl: string; authorization: string; body?: Object; message?: string; octetStream?: boo…): Promise<Object | undefined>` — Performs an HTTP request with comprehensive options for different API scenarios. This method handles all HTTP communication with the Alteryx API, supporting various content types, response formats, and error handling strategies.

- `AddVersionToWorkflow(workflowId: string, params: { file: any; name: string; ownerId: string; othersMayDownload: boolean; othersCanExecute: boolean; executionMode: string; makePublished: boolean; comments?: str…): Promise<SDKModels.WorkflowView>` — Adds a new version to an existing workflow by uploading a new workflow package file. This method enables versioning of workflows, allowing for: Updating workflows with new functionality Maintaining multiple versions of the same workflow Optionally publishing the new version as the current active version Versioning is a key feature for workflow management as it allows for: Testing new versions without affecting production Rolling back to previous versions if issues are found Maintaining an audit trail of workflow changes Add a new version to an existing workflow WorkflowManagementClient
- `CreateWorkflow(params?: { file: any; name: string; ownerId: string; isPublic: boolean; isReadyForMigration: boolean; othersMayDownload: boolean; othersCanExecute: boolean; executionMod…): Promise<string>` — Creates a new workflow in Alteryx Server by uploading a workflow package file along with metadata and permission settings. This method handles the complex process of uploading a workflow file and configuring its properties, including: Basic metadata (name, owner, comments) Permission settings (public access, execution rights, download rights) Execution configuration (execution mode, credential requirements) Collection assignments Worker and district tags for execution routing The workflow file should be an Alteryx workflow package (.yxzp or .yxmd file). Upload a new workflow to Alteryx Server WorkflowManagementClient
- `DeleteWorkflow(workflowId: string, force?: boolean): Promise<Response>` — Permanently deletes a workflow from Alteryx Server. This method removes a workflow and all its versions from the server. This is a destructive operation that cannot be undone, so it should be used with caution. If the workflow is associated with schedules, the operation will fail by default. Setting the force parameter to true will delete all associated schedules before deleting the workflow. Common use cases include: Removing obsolete or unused workflows Cleaning up test workflows Removing workflows that have been migrated to other systems Permanently delete a workflow and all its versions WorkflowManagementClient
- `DownloadWorkflow(workflowId: string, versionId?: string, options?: any): Promise<Response>` — Downloads a workflow package file from Alteryx Server. This method retrieves the actual workflow file (.yxzp or .yxmd) that can be: Saved to disk for backup purposes Imported into Alteryx Designer for editing Uploaded to another Alteryx Server instance Used for version control or archiving By default, this method downloads the published (active) version of the workflow. You can specify a particular version by providing the versionId parameter. The response is a raw binary file that should be handled appropriately by the client. Download a workflow package file WorkflowManagementClient
- `GetJobsForWorkflow(workflowId: string, sortField?: string, direction?: string, offset?: string, limit?: string, options?: any): Promise<Array<SDKModels.WorkflowJobView>>` — Retrieves the execution history (jobs) for a specific workflow. This method returns information about past and current executions of a workflow, including status, start/end times, and execution parameters. It supports pagination and sorting to handle large numbers of job records efficiently. Common use cases include: Monitoring workflow execution history Auditing workflow usage Troubleshooting failed workflow executions Analyzing workflow performance over time Retrieve execution history for a workflow WorkflowManagementClient
- `GetWorkflow(workflowId: string): Promise<SDKModels.WorkflowView>` — Retrieves detailed information about a specific workflow by its ID. This method fetches comprehensive information about a workflow, including: Basic metadata (name, description, creation date) Owner information Permission settings Version information Execution settings This is typically used to: Display workflow details to users Check workflow configuration before execution Verify workflow settings before making changes Retrieve a complete workflow record by ID WorkflowManagementClient
- `GetWorkflows(params?: { view?: "Default" | "Full"; name?: string; ownerId?: string; createdAfter?: string; createdBefore?: string }): Promise<Array<SDKModels.ReducedWorkflowView>>` — Retrieves a list of workflows with optional filtering criteria. This method provides a powerful way to search and filter workflows based on various criteria such as name, owner, and creation date. It's commonly used for: Displaying workflow listings in user interfaces Finding workflows that match specific criteria Building workflow dashboards and reports The method returns a reduced view of workflows by default, which includes basic information but not all details. For complete workflow information, use the 'Full' view parameter or call GetWorkflow() with a specific workflow ID. Retrieve a filtered list of workflows WorkflowManagementClient
- `UpdateWorkflow(workflowId: string, updateWorkflowContract: SDKModels.UpdateWorkflowContract): Promise<SDKModels.WorkflowView>` — Updates the metadata and settings of an existing workflow. This method allows modifying various aspects of a workflow without uploading a new workflow file or creating a new version. It's commonly used to: Change the workflow name or description Update permission settings Transfer ownership to another user Modify execution settings Note: To change the workflow owner (ownerId), the new owner must be in the same subscription as the current owner. This restriction ensures that workflows remain within their licensing boundaries. Update metadata and settings of an existing workflow WorkflowManagementClient
- `workflowsGetWorkflowQuestions(workflowId: string, versionId?: string, options: any = {}): Promise<Array<SDKModels.WorkflowQuestionView>>` — Retrieves the questions defined in a workflow. Alteryx workflows can include questions that prompt users for input values when the workflow is executed. This method retrieves those questions, which can be used to: Build dynamic user interfaces for workflow execution Understand what inputs a workflow requires Prepare data for workflow execution Questions can include various types such as text inputs, dropdowns, file selectors, and more. Each question has properties like name, type, description, and default value. Retrieve the questions defined in a workflow WorkflowManagementClient
- `GetAppInfoV1(appId: string): Promise<Response>` — Retrieve the app that was requested WorkflowManagementClientV1
- `GetAppQuestionsV1(appId: string): Promise<Array<SDKModelsV1.QuestionApiView>>` — Only app workflows can be used. Get the questions for the given Alteryx Analytics App WorkflowManagementClientV1
- `GetJobsForAppV1(appId: string, sortField?: string, direction?: string, offset?: string, limit?: string): Promise<Array<SDKModelsV1.JobListApiView>>` — Only app workflows can be used. Returns the jobs for the given Alteryx Analytics App WorkflowManagementClientV1
- `GetStudioAppsV1(sortField?: string, direction?: string, offset?: number, limit?: number, search?: string, packageType?: string): Promise<Array<SDKModelsV1.WorkflowApiView>>` — Subscription is tied to API key. You cannot request workflows for any other subscription without that subscription's key. Finds workflows in a subscription WorkflowManagementClientV1
- `PostNewJobV1(appId: string, values: SDKModelsV1.AppValues): Promise<SDKModelsV1.JobApiView>` — Use the status request to get the results of the job. Queues a job execution for the specified workflow with the supplied answers WorkflowManagementClientV1

- `GetTenant(): any`

- `HttpAction(: { verb: "GET" | "POST" | "PATCH" | "PUT" | "DELETE"; gateway: string; baseUrl: string; authorization: string; body?: Object; message?: string; octetStream?: boo…): Promise<Object | undefined>` — Performs an HTTP request to the Alteryx API through the configured authenticator. This method delegates the HTTP request to the authenticator's HttpAction method, which ensures that all requests are properly authenticated. The authenticator handles token renewal, request formatting, and error handling. This design pattern centralizes authentication logic and ensures consistent handling of API requests across all SDK client classes.

### TokenRotation

File: `src/api/alteryx-base.ts`

Description: TokenRotation interface marks all classes which rotate the authentication token according to ayx-node specifications. TokenRotation

Methods:
- `GetGateway(): string` — returns the currently used ayx-node gateway TokenRotation
- `GetTenant(): string` — returns the currently used ayx-node tenant TokenRotation
- `GetToken(): Promise<string>` — Returns the current token TokenRotation
- `HttpAction(: { verb: "GET" | "POST" | "PATCH" | "PUT" | "DELETE"; gateway: string; baseUrl: string; authorization: string; body?: Object; message?: string; octetStream?: boo…): Promise<Object | undefined>`
- `RenewToken(): Promise<boolean>` — Checks if the token has expired and renews it if necessary. TokenRotation

## Public functions

- `addAndStoreConfiguration(configuration: any)` — Processes and stores a credentials configuration. This function: Validates the configuration Normalizes gateway URLs Encrypts credentials if a passkey is provided Ensures exactly one credential is selected as default Stores the configuration to auth.json
  Defined in `src/api/utils.ts`
- `checkList(list)` — Ensures exactly one credential in a list is marked as selected (default). If multiple or no credentials are selected, this function will select the first credential in the list as the default.
  Defined in `src/api/utils.ts`
- `checksumFile(hashName: string, path: string): Promise<string>` — Calculates a cryptographic hash (checksum) of a file. This function streams the file contents to avoid loading the entire file into memory, making it suitable for large files.
  Defined in `src/api/utils.ts`
- `getFullConfig(): { credentials: authJson[] }` — Gets the full authentication configuration from auth.json. If the file or directory doesn't exist, it creates them with an empty configuration. This function is used to retrieve stored credentials for authentication.
  Defined in `src/api/utils.ts`
- `getPasskeyForUnitTest(): string` — passkey for unit tests. if the environment variable is not set it is using the default passkey.
  Defined in `test/test-utils.ts`
- `isClientCredentials(obj: any): boolean`
  Defined in `src/api/sdk/common/credentials.ts`
- `isGuid(x: string): boolean` — Validates if a string is a valid GUID/UUID. This function checks if the string matches the standard UUID format: xxxxxxxx-xxxx-Mxxx-Nxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx Where M is 1-5 (version) and N is 8-b (variant)
  Defined in `src/api/utils.ts`
- `isSecretCredentials(obj: any): boolean`
  Defined in `src/api/sdk/common/credentials.ts`
- `isTokenCredentials(obj: any): boolean`
  Defined in `src/api/sdk/common/credentials.ts`
- `isTokenRotation(obj: any): boolean` — Type guard function to check if an object implements the TokenRotation interface. This function performs a comprehensive check to ensure the object has all required methods of the TokenRotation interface and that they are actually functions. This is used primarily in the SdkClient constructor to determine the type of authentication mechanism provided.
  Defined in `src/api/alteryx-base.ts`
- `isUserCredentials(obj: any): boolean`
  Defined in `src/api/sdk/common/credentials.ts`
- `pruneCert(s: string): string` — Removes certificate header and footer lines from a certificate string. This function is used to clean certificate strings by removing the "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----" and "-----END CERTIFICATE-----" lines.
  Defined in `src/api/utils.ts`
- `truncate(_string: string, limit: number)` — Truncates a string to a specified length, adding ellipsis if necessary. If the string is shorter than the limit, it pads the string to reach the limit.
  Defined in `src/api/utils.ts`

- `normalizePasskey: unknown = (passkey: string): string => { return passkey.length < 32 ? passkey + new Array(33 - passkey.length).join("$") : passkey.substr(0, 32); }` — Normalizes a passkey to ensure it's exactly 32 characters long as required by AES-256. If the passkey is shorter than 32 characters, it's padded with '$' characters. If longer, it's truncated to 32 characters.
  Defined in `src/api/utils.ts`
